designVsCode.note: Each row attributes the 2026-08-05 inspection findings to the side of the system they belong to. States are in-place / partial / absent, and every cell carries the measurement it rests on.

design.detail: 127 in-scope components in the UI Kit; Wellpass design coverage at 100%

Measured, not just specified: 18 of 20 token pairs pass WCAG AA and 11 reach AAA, with the only two below the threshold being disabled text, which WCAG exempts. 94% of stateful components model a focus state. The contribution checklist gates WCAG 2.2 AA on every new component.

code.detail: Zero axe assertions. The a11y gate is set to test: todo. Storybook accessibility tests have never run because vitest.config.ts points at two paths that do not exist. eo-link fails WCAG 4.1.2 and 2.1.1.

design.detail: Two-track process documented and practised across v0.0.14 to v0.0.25, with migration guides and a six-week deprecation grace period

code.detail: 0 git tags, 0 releases, no CHANGELOG; the version is a CI build counter

design.detail: Measured across all 109,402 layers: 0.54% generic names, zero detached instances, 96% of fills and 100% of strokes bound to variables (98.6% of fills once icon placeholders are excluded)

code.detail: 14 of 15 components follow the house pattern; nothing enforces it — no lint rule catches a deviation

accessibility.headline: Specified, measured and passing on the design side. Unverified on the code side.
accessibility.source: WCAG contrast computed directly from the token system across both brand modes, plus focus-state coverage across the UI Kit

contrast.exemptNote: The only two pairs below 4.5:1 are disabled text at 2.1:1. WCAG 1.4.3 explicitly exempts inactive controls from the contrast minimum, so every pair that the guideline actually governs passes.
contrast.caveat: The EGYM accent pairs land on exactly 4.5:1 — passing, but with no headroom. Any darkening of the surface or lightening of the accent breaks them.

focusStates.note: Of the components that model interaction states at all, 94% include a focus state. Most of those without a state property are containers — cards, navigation shells, button stacks — where the interaction lives in the child.

designSide.gate: WCAG 2.2 AA is a mandatory phase in the contribution checklist: ARIA Authoring Practices, keyboard paths, contrast ratios, 44x44 touch targets, reduced motion and screen-reader testing.
designSide.open: One reported brand-on-dark AA contrast failure on free and secondary buttons, unanswered since 31 July. Dark mode is scaffolding — 7 variables against 1,111 in Brand — so this sits outside the shipped surface.

codeSide.rootCause: Two typos in vitest.config.ts point at paths that do not exist, so npm run storybook:test resolves zero projects and passes silently. Every Storybook test, including every accessibility check, has never run — found in five consecutive inspections.
codeSide.failing: eo-link renders no anchor element, is not keyboard reachable and does not announce as a link — WCAG 4.1.2 and 2.1.1.
codeSide.inProgress: delegatesFocus is now the house pattern, the tooltip enforces focusable anchors, and PR #166 adds the first behavioural focus-ring test — approved and still unmerged.

accessibility.theContrast: The design system specifies WCAG 2.2 AA, and every colour pair it governs measurably passes. The code that implements it has never run a single accessibility check.

designOpen.note: The design side is strong, not spotless. These are the open items on our side of the line — all of them small, specific and already understood.
items: Residual unbound fills
Fill binding is at 96%, or 98.6% once icon placeholders are excluded. What remains is the logo brand marks and placeholder text still sitting in accordion-item.
66 of 128 components undescribed
Half the in-scope set has no description. The 62 that do average 1,342 characters — when this team documents, it documents properly.
Properties Glossary has drifted
14 of 34 entries are spelled differently from the real Figma property, and 8 match none. Now a generatable diff rather than a manual audit.
UI Kit changelog stalled
Last real entry is 0.0.20 on 8 May, with a malformed [0.0.0] entry above it.
Semver documented, not practised
0.0.15 deprecated three components and renamed two — and shipped as a patch.
One open contrast report
Brand-on-dark AA failure on free and secondary buttons, unanswered since 31 July.
2 broken variable aliases
dimension/size/icon/default points at deleted variables in both Smart Strength modes, so icon sizing falls back on that hardware. Specific and quick to repoint.
35 undescribed variables
All recent component-level additions. The other 1,584 are described — 98% coverage.
1 broken component set
illustrative-empty-state has conflicting variant combinations, so Figma cannot read its properties at all.
One icon breaks hyphen-case
"genius weekly target" uses spaces where all 347 others use hyphens.
3 public properties still disagree

Intent on two date components, isLoading on card-class, and is user filled on input-text and input-unit. Renaming these is breaking, so it needs the scheduled track and a migration note rather than a quiet fix.

figmaAudit.source: Live audit of the EGYM One UI Kit via the Figma plugin bridge — full traversal, not a sample
figmaAudit.note: Icon glyphs carry a placeholder fill that the consuming component overrides, so they are counted separately rather than as drift. The largest remaining block is the logo component brand marks, which are arguably correct as literals.

tokenAudit.source: Live audit of the EGYM One Token System via the Figma plugin bridge
notes: Dark mode carries 7 variables against 1,111 in Brand — it is scaffolding holding the shape, not a shipped appearance.
The 35 undescribed variables are all recent component-level additions: radio-button, navigation item, list-contained, list-item studio-service, workout-progress and logo.
radio-button/selection-marker and navigation/item/padding/inline appear here but not in the v0.0.24 export the code pipeline is pinned to — which is exactly the drift the component validator flagged.

iconAudit.source: Live audit of the EGYM One Icons library via the Figma plugin bridge

documentation.changeNote: 21 components were written or rewritten to the convention: 13 that had no description, and 8 brand and product marks. A further 9 that used the older slash-separated format were upgraded. Descriptions are additive metadata — nothing structural changed.

brokenComponentSet.name: illustrative-empty-state
brokenComponentSet.detail: Figma refuses to read its property definitions — the set has conflicting or duplicate variant combinations

propertyNameCasing.note: Unchanged — this needs a variant property rename, which is a breaking change for anyone binding to the old spelling, so it was not touched.

namingOutlier.name: genius weekly target
namingOutlier.detail: Uses spaces where all 347 other public components use hyphen-case

iconAudit.note: A consumer switching an icon to filled has to know which of four spellings that particular icon uses. The four chevrons and checkmark are among the most-used icons in the set.

deepScan.source: Full traversal of all three design files via the Figma plugin bridge

localStyles.note: Zero local paint, text, effect or grid styles in either library. Everything runs through variables — the legacy style path has been fully retired.

autoLayout.note: Several of the 0% cases are legitimately static artwork — logo, focus-outline and loading-spinner are single-shape components. segmented-control at 26% across 1,680 frames is the one worth looking at.

propertyNaming.note: The form family is the worst of these: input-comment, input-password and textarea say is user-filled while input-unit and input-text say is user filled. Sibling components disagreeing is exactly what makes an API hard to learn.

iconsPropertyNaming.note: All 13 isFilled spellings aligned, and the two organisation components now agree on isChecked.
